nature-es-119.q: What mainly drives a storm surge?
nature-es-119.a: Strong winds pushing water toward the coast.

nature-es-104.q: Where did streptomycin and artemisinin come from?
nature-es-104.a: Streptomycin came from a soil bacterium; the antimalarial artemisinin came from a plant.

nature-es-107.q: Firewood is renewable, so how can it run out?
nature-es-107.a: Local demand can quickly outrun how fast trees grow back.

nature-es-095.q: What is the main agent of non-animal pollination?
nature-es-095.a: Wind, which accounts for some 98% of it.

nature-es-090.q: What is habitat manipulation in pest control?
nature-es-090.a: Changing cropping systems to favour pests' natural enemies, for example with hedgerows, shelterbelts or beetle banks.

nature-es-118.q: How is this soil-formation equation mostly solved?
nature-es-118.a: Empirically, by varying one factor while holding the others constant.

nature-es-081.q: How do mangroves help keep local fish numbers up?
nature-es-081.a: They give nursery habitat to many species, including commercial fish and crustaceans.

nature-es-043.q: What other names is well-being known by?

nature-es-036.q: What are the three components of subjective well-being?
nature-es-036.a: Affect (emotions and moods), life satisfaction (judgments about one's life) and eudaimonia (a sense of meaning and purpose).

nature-es-012.q: How does ecotourism differ from plain nature tourism?
nature-es-012.a: It aims to build tourists' appreciation of habitats and local culture.

nature-es-020.q: Who popularised forest bathing, and why?
nature-es-020.a: Tomohide Akiyama, head of Japan's forestry ministry, in 1982, to get more people into forests.

nature-es-039.q: What does responsible tourism aim for?
nature-es-039.a: To maximise benefits to local communities and minimise harmful social or environmental impacts.

nature-es-013.q: Name some ways to manage visitor impacts.
nature-es-013.a: Setting a carrying capacity, hardening sites, sustainable design, visitor quotas, fees, access limits and visitor education.

nature-es-018.q: What do the three subscales of nature relatedness measure?
nature-es-018.a: Identifying with nature, concern about human effects on the environment, and comfort and wish to be in nature.

nature-es-057.q: Why is remote sensing useful for fieldwork?
nature-es-057.a: It reaches dangerous or remote places and can replace slower, costlier fieldwork without disturbing the site.

nature-es-061.q: What are the three central ideas of agent-based models?
nature-es-061.a: Agents as objects, emergence and complexity: simple rules for agents can produce complex behaviour.

nature-es-073.q: Where has GIS-based spatial analysis spread beyond its origins?
nature-es-073.a: From ecology, geology and epidemiology to natural resources, disaster risk and climate change adaptation.

nature-es-068.a: It sends out its own light and uses the speed of light to turn the return time into distance.

nature-es-053.q: How does a union overlay differ from an intersect?
nature-es-053.a: A union keeps everything from both inputs; an intersect keeps only where they overlap.

nature-es-078.q: What does a reinforcing loop do?
nature-es-078.a: It amplifies change, as when more adopters of a product create stronger word of mouth; counteracting loops push back.

nature-es-065.q: Which tree services do these tools put numbers on?
nature-es-065.a: Pollution removal, carbon storage and avoided stormwater runoff.

nature-es-067.q: What does the Figure of Merit measure?
nature-es-067.a: As one percentage, the overlap between real and simulated land change, built from hits, misses and false alarms.

nature-val-070.q: How did Adam Smith frame the paradox of value?
nature-val-070.a: He separated 'value in use' from 'value in exchange', noting the most useful things often have little exchange value.

nature-val-062.q: What is the core principle of deep ecology?
nature-val-062.a: The living environment as a whole has basic moral and legal rights to live and flourish, apart from human use.

nature-val-064.q: How do ecocentrics see themselves differently from technocentrics?
nature-val-064.a: Ecocentrics see themselves as subject to nature and prefer low-impact technology and self-reliance; technocentrics do not see cutting industry as the solution.

nature-val-052.q: What does total economic value add up?
nature-val-052.a: The values an ecosystem provides: direct and indirect use value, plus non-use value.

nature-val-071.q: How does direct use value differ from indirect use value?
nature-val-071.a: Direct use value comes from removable products such as timber, fish and water; indirect from things like a sunset or waterfall.

nature-val-092.q: What does hedonic pricing measure in environmental work?
nature-val-092.a: How much a nearby amenity such as a park raises home prices, holding other house features fixed.

nature-val-096.q: What is this rationality test widely used for?
nature-val-096.a: In econometrics, to test whether choices are rational and to build preferences from real data.

nature-val-086.q: What did the panel recommend for contingent valuation surveys?
nature-val-086.a: Personal interviews, a yes-or-no vote on a specific tax, and detailed information about the resource and its threats.

nature-val-100.q: What does a discrete choice model give?
nature-val-100.a: The probability that a person picks a given option, based on features of the options and of the person.

nature-val-081.q: What problem does a probit model solve?
nature-val-081.a: It estimates the probability that an observation falls into one of two categories, as logistic regression also does.

nature-val-084.a: When people have less information about a good and information is costly.

nature-val-017.a: Because of externalities and because taxes, subsidies, quotas and tariffs distort market prices.

nature-val-006.q: Why can cost-benefit analysis overlook fairness?
nature-val-006.a: It treats a positive net benefit as decisive regardless of who wins and who loses.

nature-val-005.q: What did critics in the 1980s say about cost-benefit analysis of rules?
nature-val-005.a: It could serve political goals, was biased against regulation, and caused long delays.

nature-val-024.q: What is the payback period of a $1000 investment returning $500 a year?

nature-val-020.q: As a rule of thumb, when is a project worthwhile by its benefit-cost ratio?
nature-val-020.a: When benefits exceed costs; the higher the ratio, the better.

nature-val-037.q: What are the main competing views in environmental ethics besides anthropocentrism?

nature-val-049.q: What is Aldo Leopold's basic principle of the land ethic?
nature-val-049.a: A thing is right when it tends to preserve the integrity, stability and beauty of the living community.

nature-val-046.a: When no amount of one would make up for a loss of the other, as with freedom and security.

nature-val-039.q: Which famous hypothesis may belong to ecologic extension?
nature-val-039.a: James Lovelock's Gaia hypothesis, treating Earth as one whole with its own ethical value.

nature-val-032.q: Why does nature tend to be overexploited, on this view?
nature-val-032.a: Because its value cannot be fully counted in money, it is overexploited and 'underproduced'.

nature-acct-021.q: How does the UN Development Programme define human development?
nature-acct-021.a: Enlarging people's choices to live a long healthy life, be educated, have a decent living standard and enjoy freedom and self-respect.

nature-acct-010.q: What is green GDP in simple form?
nature-acct-010.a: GDP minus environmental costs minus social costs.

nature-acct-019.q: What does this approach aim to maximise instead of wealth?

nature-acct-011.q: Why did China's green GDP effort collapse in 2007?
nature-acct-011.a: Environmental adjustments cut growth to politically unacceptable levels, nearly zero in some provinces.

nature-acct-024.q: Why is ordinary national income always higher than sustainable national income?
nature-acct-024.a: It leaves out the loss of environmental functions.

nature-acct-017.q: Why do critics say GNP puts the environment on the wrong side of the ledger?
nature-acct-017.a: Polluting and then cleaning up both add to GNP.

nature-acct-089.q: What costs does environmental accounting track?
nature-acct-089.a: Resource use and costs such as cleaning up contaminated sites, fines and taxes, pollution-prevention technology and waste handling.
